subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw support LLM-driven contextual activation for unmentioned group traffic, and should that behavior live in core shared activation, a plugin/channel API seam, or a narrower attention/ambient-room mode?
rationale: Automation can prove the current gap, but cannot choose the privacy boundary, provider exposure, retained decision logs, config contract, channel coverage, or long-term ownership for processing unmentioned group traffic.

options.title: Sponsor default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

options.title: Narrow to attention or ambient behavior
options.body: Pursue timer-based attention windows or documented ambient room-event ergonomics without adding a model-driven background peeking path yet.

options.title: Defer to a plugin/API seam
options.body: Wait for or design the observation/decision-hook API needed to keep this optional policy outside core runtime defaults.

recommendation.title: Sponsor default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest history across the central activation and mention-policy code paths that the decision would extend.
